question.leadin: Identify these longtime Senators who died in 2009 or 2010.
question.text: This longest-serving Senator in U.S. history represented West Virginia in the Senate from 1959 until his death in 2010.
question.clue: This long-serving West Virginian senator who once gave a 14-hour speech to filibuster the 1964 Civil Rights Act.

swap.text: In a tweet, this South Carolina senator stated that "any policy proposal which drives up costs of Corona, tequila, or margaritas is a big-time bad idea" in response to a 20% income tax with Mexico to pay the wall.
swap.clue: This Senator, who is widely rumored to be gay, has remained low in the polls but was widely regarded as the winner of the September 16th "kid's table" debate.

question.text: This man served as Governor of Florida from 1999-2007, becoming the first two-term Republican governor in the state's history. He is the son of a former US President and the brother of another.
question.clue: Alex Sink, the Democrat defeated by Scott, now makes a historically unique household with her husband Bill McBride, who lost the 2002 Florida Gubernatorial election to this mentor of Marco Rubio.

swap.text: The first Jewish woman to serve on the Supreme Court, she served for 13 years on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit before being nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993.
swap.clue: This co-founder of the ACLU's Women's Rights Project struck down VMI's male-only admission policy as part of her longtime advocacy for women's rights.

question.leadin: Answer the following about American electoral history - as portrayed on Saturday Night Live.
question.text: One of the most lasting SNL portrayals was Tina Fey's caricature of this governor of Alaska. Fey's quote "I can see Russia from my house" has often been misattributed to this running mate of John McCain.

swap.text: This Supreme Court case struck down DOMA's third section. This case was filed after the defendant had to pay the IRS $363,053 in estate taxes after her spouse's death in 2009.
swap.clue: This case, decided on the same day as Hollingsworth v. Perry. The ruling in this case, which struck down parts of DOMA, was based on the Due Process clause of the Fifth Amendment.

question.text: Under Dukakis's governorship, this convicted felon escaped from custody after he was given a furlough. When Dukakis declined to mention the incident, Bush launched a series of advertisements raising awareness about this man.
question.clue: According to the book The Loudest Voice in the Room, Roger Stone was called "a pussy" for criticizing a piece featuring this man created by Lee Atwater.

swap.text: One possible spoiler for Clinton's nomination is this man, the Democratic former governor of Maryland. His achievements as governor include the legalization of gay marriage and making some undocumented immigrants eligible for college tuition.
swap.clue: This governor of Maryland has publicly declared interest for the 2016 Democratic nomination. He signed a 2012 law legalizing same-sex marriage in his state.

question.text: In this 2004 case, the Supreme Court ruled that U.S. citizens detained as enemy combatants must be able to challenge their detention before a neutral decision maker.

swap.text: The National Civilian Community Corps and VISTA are part of this umbrella service organization through which fifty thousand Americans meet community needs in the U.S. For 15 points, name this network of service organizations that President Clinton established on the model of the Peace Corps.

question.text: The sons of one of the founding John Birch Society members are these two brothers, who run a Kansas based conglomerate. They give lots of money to libertarian and conservative groups - particular, they were major donors to Scott Walker's campaign in Wisconsin.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people's reactions to the 2011 earthquake in Japan.
swap.text: This governor of Mississippi, considered a potential Republican presidential candidate in 2012, saw his press secretary, Dan Turner, resign after a Turner e-mail cracked that the song "(Sittin' on) the Dock of the Bay" was not popular in Japan right now.
swap.clue: This man's former lobbying firm, which is named for himself, Griffith and Rogers, may have engaged in corporate espionage on behalf of Alfa Bank.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about political scandals in the 1980s.
question.text: This Senator from Colorado withdrew his campaign for the Democratic nomination shortly after photos were released of him and Donna Rice on a yacht named Monkey Business.
question.clue: In his first campaign for his party's nomination, his opponent quoted a Wendy's commercial in asking him "Where's the beef?"

swap.leadin: Name some Republican 2008 nominees for president.
swap.text: This senator from Kansas is a total redneck who advocates complete banning of abortion and a flat tax, and wants to "renew the family".
swap.clue: This Republican Kansas governor was re-elected despite more than a hundred Republicans endorsing his Democratic opponent in response to this man's extensive, revenue-negative tax cuts.

question.text: At the beginning of 2012, you gave the Tea Party's response to Obama's State of the Union address. Your speech was assuredly better than the official GOP response, delivered by this Governor of Indiana.
question.clue: This former CEO of the Hudston Institute was nicknamed "The Blade" for his tenacity at budget-cutting as head of the Office of Management and Budget.

swap.leadin: According to a sketch on SNL, it includes Enron, the economy, Tom Daschle, Japan, Germany, Italy, Dick Cheney, and Evil Knievel, but usually it's just Iran, Iraq, and North Korea. FTPE, identify.
swap.text: This phrase, first used by George W. Bush in his 2002 State of the Union Address.
swap.clue: According to Condoleeza Rice, members "are repressive regimes that are opaque," "have been very, very harsh on their people," and "are aggressively seeking weapons of mass destruction."

question.text: The prosecution in the Clinton impeachment was led by this powerful Illinois Republican, the Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee. During the trial, it was revealed that this man had an extramarital affair of his own during the 1960's.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about US gubernatorial elections in 2013.
swap.text: In New Jersey, this female state senator is the most likely Democratic nominee to run against Republican Chris Christie.

question.text: Siegel was shot in the home of this woman, his alleged girlfriend and a renowned depositor of money for the mob. After she refused to snitch as a star witness in front of the Kefauver committee, she punched several reporters on her way out, exclaiming "I hope an atom bomb falls on all of you!"

swap.text: Although viewed by conservatives as a right-wing vote, Souter voted with the majority in this case, which ruled that schools could not sponsor clerics in even non-denominational prayers. This case dealt with a rabbi delivering a prayer at a graduation ceremony.
